# local 0004: mcs51: compiler crash for functions with a function attribute that return a struct and have a non-struct first parameter

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Make the front end and aopArg agree on register parameters of functions that return a struct.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The compiler crashes with a segmentation fault for the file below. It was compiled with
`sdcc -mmcs51 -c r1.c` on r17176, and the compiler printed `Caught signal 11: SIGSEGV`. In a
backtrace from gdb, the fault is in `genMove_o` in `src/mcs51/gen.c`, which `genReceive` calls
through `genMove` with a null pointer as the source.

```c
struct s { unsigned char a; int b; unsigned char c; };

struct s r1 (unsigned char x) __reentrant
{
  struct s r;
  r.a = x;
  r.b = 1;
  r.c = 2;
  return r;
}
```

The compiler also crashes with `--stack-auto`, with `--model-large`, and with both options. It
crashes with `__critical` or `__using (0)` in the place of `__reentrant` as well.

The function compiles without `__reentrant`, and it compiles without the keyword under
`--stack-auto` as well. A `__reentrant` function with the parameter list `(void)` compiles too,
and so does one whose first parameter is a struct.

## Cause

The iCode of `r1` has a `RECEIVE` for `x`, which means that the front end has marked `x` as a
register parameter. `genReceive` asks `aopArg` for the registers of the parameter. `aopArg`
returns 0 for every parameter of functions that return a struct, because the registers stay free
for the hidden pointer to the result. `genReceive` passes the result to `genMove` without a check.

The origin of the mark was observed in gdb on r17176, with a breakpoint on `_mcs51_regparm` in
`src/mcs51/main.c`. In `src/SDCC.y` the rule `declarator2_function_attributes` appends the
attribute to the declarator with `addDecl`, and `addDecl` calls `processFunc` in
`src/SDCCsymt.c`. The return type is not in the function type at that time, so `_mcs51_regparm`
finds no struct and returns 1 for the first parameter. `processFunc` runs twice more when the
return type is known, and `_mcs51_regparm` returns 0 in both runs. The mark of the first run
stays, because `processFunc` sets `SPEC_REGPARM` and has no code that clears it. This last point
was read from the source.

## Related

Bug #3847 concerns functions that return the struct value of a call. This defect was found with
its test cases, and the patch for that bug, applied to r17176, does not change it.
